note: revision 2026-10-26-comet-050-adoption-v1: existing CI scheduled workflows / host timers only trigger the SAME original Comet maintenance entry; the trigger owns no business state or retry scheduling, no resident controller service is started, and the supervisor remains process-level restart of the original instance only. Comet itself recovers its own transactions, compensation and retries. The supervisor never becomes a second control plane.

schedulerInvocation.basis: docs/architecture/comet-ai-devops-convergence.md: reuse existing CI scheduled tasks / host timers to trigger the original command; the trigger owns no business state or retry scheduling.

ciScheduledWorkflow.note: the scheduling capability exists on the platform, but no committed workflow carries a schedule trigger today; registering one is a repository change that must update this registration in the same change, never an invention here.

hostTimer.note: host timer facilities exist on the host, but this repository registers no timer (installer surface tools/hooks/scripts carries none); nothing here installs one.

invocationContract.originalEntryNote: the real maintenance command wiring (knowledge revocation maintenance operations, permission maintenance) belongs to P4_8/pilot runs; this mapping declares WHAT a timer may invoke, not that a timer is wired.
invocationContract.note: a registered timer may only invoke the same original Comet maintenance command entry used for manual permission maintenance; before any recovery invocation the old writer must be checked (startGate); no resident controller/monitor service is started by this domain.

restartBudget.basis: recommended at most 3 restarts within 5 minutes; beyond that the supervisor stops and escalates to the platform on-call.

recoveryBasis: recommended: the original instance recovers and begins reconciliation within 10 minutes; this is not a 5-minute isolation guarantee during the fault window.

startGate.note: no concurrent recovery writes while the old process is unconfirmed-terminated or the storage ownership is unknown; a second business owner is never started.

authorityBinding.note: after recovery the original authority/RunID still has exactly one business owner; authorityId is pinned only when a real runner exists.

cometSelfRecovery.note: transaction recovery, compensation and retries belong to Comet; the supervisor must not maintain a second retry loop for missed permissions.

audit.note: restarting the original instance and stopping the old writer are audited as separate events.
